content.title: About
content.content: Eggs are a food product obtained from female birds, primarily chickens. They are a versatile ingredient in cooking, used raw, boiled, fried, baked, and in a wide range of baked goods.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Eggs are one of the most affordable and widely available sources of complete protein.
Chicken eggs contain all essential amino acids needed by humans.
Eggshell color (white, brown, blue) depends on the breed of the hen.
The yolk’s color varies with the hen’s diet; more carotenoids produce a deeper orange hue.
Eggs can be stored in the refrigerator for 3–5 weeks; freshness can be tested by placing them in water—fresh eggs sink, older ones float.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: A single egg provides about 6 g of protein that includes all essential amino acids, supporting muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Egg yolks are a good source of vitamins B12, B2 (riboflavin) and B5, which are important for energy metabolism and nervous system health.

items.title: Source of vitamins D and A
items.content: Eggs are one of the few natural food sources of vitamin D, and they also contain vitamin A, which supports vision and immune function.

items.title: Contains choline
items.content: Choline in the yolk is essential for brain function, fat metabolism, and liver health.

items.title: Eye‑protecting antioxidants
items.content: Lutein and zeaxanthin, present in the yolk, help protect the eyes from age‑related macular degeneration.

items.title: Egg allergy
items.content: Some individuals are allergic to eggs, experiencing reactions ranging from skin rashes to anaphylaxis.

items.title: Cholesterol content
items.content: Egg yolks contain cholesterol; people with high cholesterol levels should consume them in moderation.

items.title: Salmonella risk
items.content: Raw eggs can be contaminated with Salmonella; proper refrigeration and thorough cooking reduce this risk.

items.title: Consuming raw eggs
items.content: Eating raw or undercooked eggs increases the chance of foodborne illness, especially in children, pregnant women, and immunocompromised individuals.

items.title: Storage and shelf life
items.content: Eggs should be kept refrigerated, unwashed, in their original carton to preserve the protective cuticle. Discard any egg with an off smell or unusual appearance.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Eggs can be boiled (hard‑ or soft‑boiled), fried, scrambled, made into omelets, used in baking, turned into sauces like mayonnaise, and added to salads. Egg whites are also popular in protein shakes and low‑fat dishes.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store eggs in their carton in the refrigerator at 1–4 °C. They remain fresh for about 3–5 weeks. If an egg smells sour, has a discolored yolk, or leaks, it should be discarded.
